full_judgment:
Mr. Sharif Uddin Chaklader, J: This appeal by the plaintiff directed against judgment and order dated 5.3.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 2007 thereby rejecting the application filed under order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. Short facts for disposal of the appeal are that, plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.20 of  1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kochua, Chandpur against the defendant-respondent-opposite patties for permanent injunction. Defendants contested the suit by filing written statement. Learned Assistant Judge framed 5 issues and on consideration of the depositions of the witnesses, 8 for plaintiff and 7 for defendants decreed the suit. Against this judgment, defendants preferred Title Appeal No.172 of 1997 in the Court of District Judge, Chandpur and the appeal was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur for disposal. After hearing the appeal the learned Joint District Judge set aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge and remanded the suit back to the trial Court for fresh decision by judgment and decree dated 26.11.2002. Learned Assistant Judge again decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 14.2.2005. Defendants preferred Title Appeal No.21 of 2005 in the Court of District Judge, Chandpur who transferred the appeal for disposal to the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur who heard the appeal repartee and pronounced the judgment allowing the appeal by judgment and decree dated 28.6.2007. Thereafter, plaintiff filed application under Order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure which gave rise to Miscellaneous Case 'No.11 of 2007. Learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur by the impugned order dated 25.5.2008 dismissed the Miscellaneous Case and rejected the application for re-hearing of the appeal. 

 3. Mr. S. N. Goswami, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant, submits that, the impugned judgment and order having been passed without any basis is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate further submits that learned Joint District Judge did not apply his judicial mind to the facts made out in the application under order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure and did not at all consider the law as such committed error of law and fact in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case. Learned Advocate further submits that plaintiff-appellant is in possession of the schedule land as described in the plaint and defendants have no possession far less exclusive in the suit land as such the application under order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure ought to be disposed of in accordance with law. 

 4. Mr. M. A. Quayyum Chowdhury, learned Advocate, appearing for the respondents, on the other hand, submits that, the appeal was dismissed within the very knowledge of the plaintiff as such the order passed by the learned Joint District Judge dismissing the Miscellaneous Case having been within his jurisdiction calls for no interference. Learned Advocate further submits that from the order sheet and also from the fact together with the application, the proceeding of the appeal was continue' within the knowledge of the plaintiff but they in order to delay in disposal of the suit did not appeared at the time of hearing of the appeal and take dilatory tactics in the matter of enjoying the suit property by the defendant-appellant-respondents as such, the learned Advocate further submits, that Order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the facts of this suit and appeal is not maintainable, teamed Judge having observed the conduct of the plaintiff and respondents before this Court dismissed the Miscellaneous Case and rejected the application for re-hearing of the appeal. 

 7. On a study of these orders it appears that respondent did not appear when the appeal was received by the learned Joint District Judge. It appears that Miscellaneous Case No.1 I of 2007 was filed under Order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure within the prescribed period of time, Order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure speaks as `where an appeal is heard ex parte and judgment is pronounced against the respondent, 'he may apply to the Appellate Court to re-hear the appeal; if he satisfies the Court that the notice was not duly served or that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the appeal was called on for hearing the Court shall re-hear the appeal on such terms as to costs or otherwise as it thinks fit to impose upon him'. It appears from the aforesaid orders that when the appeal was transferred to the Court of the Joint District Judge for disposal respondents in any of the dates were not present. It strike my mind as to why the learned Joint District Judge was so hurry in disposing of the appeal as on the date of receiving of the appeal from the teamed District Judge, learned Judge heard the appeal even finding that respondent was not present. It appears that respondent was not present till pronouncement of judgment. I do not understand how the learned Judge totally disregards the provision of law. Learned Judge did not at all satisfy as to whether notice of transfer of the appeal to his Court was served upon the plaintiff or upon the teamed Advocate for the respondents. Judge who hurried in disposing of cases are not sound in mind. Justice hurried Justice buried. It is to be borne in mind court is to render Justice and that too, not only done but act impartially so that it can be shown so that trust, faith and believe of the litigant may not be disturbed. From the impugned order I did not find respondent appeared in the Court. I find substance in this appeal. 

 9. The impugned judgment and order dated 25.5.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur in Miscellaneous Case No.11 of 2007 is set aside. I also set aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No.21 of 2005 on 28.6.2007. Title Appeal No.21 of 2005 is restored to its file and number.
